senses.gloss:
लौकाक्ष लौकाक्ष, आस्, m. pl., N. of a
school, (perhaps for लौगाक्ष.)

लौकायतिक लौकायतिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr.
लोकायत), following the teaching of Cārvāka; (अस्),
m. a follower of Cārvāka, a materialist, atheist.

लौकिक लौकिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. लोक), worldly,
mundane, terrestrial, popular, familiar (as opposed to
अ-लौकिक, ‘technical’), belonging to ordinary life,
occurring in every-day life, vulgar, common, usual,
ordinary, fashionable, publicly received, customary,
temporal, secular, not sacred (as opposed to वैदिक,
आर्ष, शास्त्रीय); belonging to the world of (at the
end of a comp., e. g. ब्रह्म-लौकिक, belonging
to the world of Brahmā); (आस्), m. pl. common or
ordinary men (as opposed to ‘the learned, initiated,’
&c.), men in general, the human race; men familiar
with the ways of the world, men of the world;
(अम्), n. anything occurring in the world, the laws
or ordinances of the world, general custom, usage.
—लौकिक-ता, f. or लौकिक-त्व, अम्, n. worldli-
ness, commonness, worldly currency or custom, popu-
larity, usual custom, usage, general prevalence.
—लौ-
किक-विषय-विचार, अस्, m. ‘consideration of ordi-
nary objects, ‘N. of a philosophical treatise.

लौक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the world,
being in the world, extended through the world,
generally diffused, worldly, mundane, terrestrial,
human, general, ordinary, common, common-place;
(अस्), m. a proper N.
